regime: De-Risk / Pre-CPI Rollover (NQ, ES, gold flip short)
summary: Broad de-risk day with nothing on the US calendar and July CPI one day out. This was not yesterday's rotation. Today everything came off the table together. NQ sold the open and closed 29,647.25 (-0.39%), below both its trend stop and its average, a fresh short. The S&P did the same, losing its stop and flipping short at 7,753.25 (-0.31%), so the split between the two indices is over. Even gold, the week's strongest trend, rejected an overnight spike to 4,461.9 and reversed all session to close 4,394.8 (-0.49%), flipping its own trend short. Crude was the lone gainer, up +1.15% to 83.24, but it faded from an 84.64 high and closed just under its stop, capped. The VIX actually eased to 15.28 (-1.16%) and the 10-year yield slipped, so this was an orderly flattening into the print, not a panic. Traders reduced exposure across the board ahead of Wednesday's inflation number.
psychology: Today was about how you handle the day before a known catalyst, and about not marrying yesterday's winner. Twenty-four hours ago gold was the hero of the tape, the cleanest trend on the board. Today it rejected a new high and flipped short. That is the market reminding you that trends end, and the session before a big print is exactly when crowded trades get unwound. If you were still leaning long gold because it worked yesterday, today cost you. The discipline into an event like CPI is simple: carry less, not more. There is no edge in guessing the number, and the first move after an 8:30 print is often a head-fake that reverses once the real positioning shows up. The professional play is patience. Let the print land, wait for the market to accept beyond a level with two hourly closes, and trade the reaction. Guessing the number is gambling. Trading the reaction is a plan.

event.name: No scheduled release: markets flatten into CPI
event.consensus: No top-tier US release was scheduled for Tuesday, August 11. The week's main event is the July CPI report on Wednesday, August 12 at 8:30 AM ET.
event.actual: With nothing on the calendar, the session was about positioning ahead of CPI, and traders took risk off across the board. The Nasdaq and S&P both sold the open and flipped their trend stops short, and even gold, the week's strongest trend, rejected an overnight high and flipped short. This was a broad de-risk, not a rotation.
event.surprise: The VIX eased to 15.28 (-1.16%) and the 10-year yield slipped to about 4.69%, so this was an orderly flattening rather than a fear-driven sell-off. Positioning came off before the number, not in a panic.
event.nqReaction: NQ opened below its average, broke down out of its opening range at 16:30 UTC, and sold off to a 29,533 low before closing 29,647.25, below both its trend stop and its average, a fresh short.
event.crossAsset: Gold gave back its overnight spike to 4,461.9 and closed 4,394.8 (-0.49%), flipping short. Crude was the lone gainer, up +1.15% to 83.24, but it faded from an 84.64 high and closed just under its trend stop, capped. The message across assets was the same: reduce exposure into the CPI print.

Three of the four opening ranges broke DOWN first (NQ, ES, and gold), and only crude broke up. That is the mirror image of yesterday and the tell that sellers ran the session. NQ's opening range was very wide at 206.75 points, about 2.47 times its 83.8 ATR, so it took until 16:30 UTC to break, and when it did the down-move extended straight to the 29,533 low.

HTA OPEN eligibility Wednesday: it is a CPI day and a Wednesday, so BIR (skips CPI), HOF (skips Wednesday), and MID (skips Wednesday) are all ineligible. Only BNC is eligible, and even then a CPI open is the highest-variance session of the week. Eligibility note, not a trade instruction.

But it could not hold the extension: it reversed all session, closed 4,394.8 (-0.49%), and flipped its own trend stop short. The targets hit, but the trend-up bias failed by the close.

Score: 5 rows, 3 triggered, 2 played out, 1 mixed, 0 failed, 2 not triggered. A broad de-risk day. The NQ and ES downside scenarios played out cleanly as both flipped short, gold tagged its upside targets overnight but reversed and flipped short too (mixed), and crude held its average and ran the opposite way.
